en: Verses on the *Guhyapadas-mahābalavikurvaṇa-rāja-sūtra*,
composed by the Great Master of Guangfu, the Chief Monk Guan Zhuba.
I take refuge in the Supreme Vehicle, And according to the Sūtra, enter into its circulation.
May I, together with all sentient beings, Realize the light within it as one.
With a mind of vast merit free from anxiety, The illusory body emerges through the four modes of birth;
Having studied the scriptures in my youth, I have forgotten the principle of True Suchness.
Attentively dwell upon the scriptural teachings, And morning and evening contemplate their essential meaning.
If the mind is clouded and you have not yet understood, Devote every thought to cultivation and refinement,
Without allowing for even a moment’s interruption.
If one does not seek the ultimate truth, when will the light of the four great elements ever reappear?
Now that we have encountered the Great Awakened Honored One, who has extensively opened the gates of skillful means,
he has carved the woodblocks to bestow these Sanskrit scriptures, spreading them far and wide like pieces of an incomplete jade disk.
Before long, in the space of a moment, the eight directions, both far and near, were all graced by the Perfectly Enlightened One; this was through the power of the Buddha’s compassion.
Though one may realize the principle of ultimate emptiness, the myriad practices have not yet been completed.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time have taught that the Tathāgata’s one great matter arises entirely from sentient beings;
if sentient beings were free from greed and anger, for what reason would the Buddhas preach, employing provisional practices and true transformations to edify them?
From his initial birth until his parinirvāṇa, within the golden outer coffin and silver inner casket,
the devas and humans of the fourfold assembly wept.
The evil spirit-king Śikhin slaughtered and cooked [beings] to establish a kingdom, where sentient beings were devoured.
Our Buddha appeared once more in this world as the Blue-Black Eight-Armed King;
with his hands grasping eight objects, he struck down this māra, who then took refuge.
Sentient beings were spared from calamity through the supreme compassion of the Equal Awakened One.
He bestowed the prophecy upon the evil Māra, along with his ministers and retinue;
through many kalpas of pure dhyāna, the assembly gathered like an ocean attained awakening.
Through provisional manifestations of wrathful power, they were executed within the Lotus Treasury World.
Never giving rise to evil thoughts—this is the gate of the Buddha’s compassion;
through holding this in mind, it shall not be in vain.
Having already perceived the limit of True Suchness (Tathatā), one should seek only worldly matters.
Without fruit, there is no fulfillment;
vain toil makes success difficult to attain. To exhort the dull-witted toward high wisdom is not a deceptive word.
If you do not speak the truth, may you enter the Hell of the Ball Game.
The four great precious seal-inscriptions are the great empowered Vajra-mind;
upon the six seals of the fingers and nails, they must not be distorted or bent.
I now explain the intent of the sutras: during the period of the Final Dharma remaining in the world, he shall protect the Teaching and protect the sovereign.
In the future world of Maitreya, throughout the periods of the True, Semblance, and Final Dharmas, he shall manifest as a single body according to the various types of beings.
Fundamental wisdom transforms into subsequent wisdom; the manifested Buddha proclaims the secret words.
The Great Expedient One transforms into the Successor King; the Successor King records his compassion.
May the meaning within these scriptures be attained, so that all sentient beings may awaken.
Diligently attending and paying homage from dawn until dusk, my mindfulness never ceases for a moment.
As I read and contemplate the Great Avataṃsaka Sūtra, I find no one who can fully unravel its principles;
only when the bhikṣu Haidiāng questioned me did I finally realize the intent of the Buddha of Compassion.
The Buddha has opened the Supreme Vehicle, Into which all people may enter.
He printed this scripture and bestowed it upon all quarters; The Great Awakened One originally has no words.
Moment by moment, he aids those according to their kind, Through the actions of body, speech, and mind.
There was never a moment of weariness or indolence;
none dared to set brush to paper. Without obscuring the principle of True Suchness (Tathatā), [this shall endure] for ten thousand years of the Dharma-ending age.
The Three Jewels bear witness, neither increasing nor decreasing;
the eight classes of beings, majestic and awe-inspiring, constantly provide protection.

Of the pure Kṣatriya lineage of the Ikṣvāku clan, he serves as the great causal condition for the transmission of the Dharma during the Final Age. By the banks of the Bahudā River, beneath the twin trees, he entered the samādhi of parinirvāṇa; the eight classes of beings were filled with grief, and the lords of the world wailed and fell prostrate.

The kings of all nations came to the Buddha’s assembly at the same time; beating their breasts and stamping their feet, they wept with choked sobs and prostrated themselves. Their cries shook the three realms, darkening the light of the sun and moon, while grievous clouds and dismal mists gathered, mountains collapsed, the earth split apart, and a great roar resounded.

The birds cry out in grief, the grasses and trees wither and dry up; the springs run dry and the ocean waves surge upward; among all things and forms, there is none that does not don mourning garments; even the Arhats and Śrāvakas do not understand the principle of ultimate truth.

The Bodhisattva masters the principle of transformation and realizes impermanence; he dwells in meditation like space, neither arising nor ceasing, yet remains within the realm of delusion to moisten and sustain rebirth. Only when the leaves of the twelve links of dependent origination have fallen does one perceive his traces.

All wriggling and sentient beings inherently possess the Buddha-nature; the deities of the three realms hasten forward to offer worship at Nirvana. The great emperors grieve with longing for the Tathāgata, while Śikhin treats the matter with contempt, deliberating on how to dispatch immortals to fetch him.

The devas then dispatched powerful mantra-masters to seize him; each wielding a precious vajra, they bound the Māra king and departed. As soon as he smelled their foul odor, he was locked away within a prison and surrounded; there was no way to take him back before the devas arrived to pay their respects.

May the Buddha, out of his great compassion, mercifully accept us; for demons and malevolent spirits afflict this region, devouring living beings and seizing young maidens to enjoy their pleasures. May the Buddha transform them so that they submit and turn toward the Dharma, even as their accumulated bones rise like mountains.

After the Tathāgata entered parinirvāṇa, the kings wept aloud; arrogant and conceited evil spirits showed no reverence or faith, and the celestial septs sent down immortals who did not return for seven days; filled with sorrow and distress, they shed tears as they came to pay homage to the golden coffin and the physical remains.

The Benevolent Father, who accords with humanity, has entered quiescent extinction; because sentient beings commit evil, the Demon King has appeared. Śikhin causes suffering and harm, devouring the flesh of sentient beings; we pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will remove this malevolent lord of beings.

The Buddha of Fundamental Wisdom eternally delights in the light of quiescence; subsequently, the Wisdom of Subsequent Attainment manifests as a form with three heads and eight arms, standing upright. He brandishes the *samantabhadra-mudrā* (all-gathering seal), the fire-wheel, and the vajra. With two arms encircled by eight dragons, he holds a lasso and rings. His right hands are as follows: the first performs the mountain-opening seal (*parvata-vivaraṇa-mudrā*), the second holds a vajra, the third holds a precious bell, and the fourth holds a spear with a precious seal. His left hands are as follows: the first performs the all-gathering seal, the second holds a fire-wheel, the third holds a lasso, and the fourth holds a precious sword.

With nine eyes and three faces, holding a sharp sword, a jewel seal, and a trident, his hair is blackish-blue and matted, with the tips standing upright and red; then the Buddha proclaimed the mantra, manifesting a great radiance so brilliant that immeasurable Māra kings all came to pay their respects.

With arms accustomed to jeweled bracelets and feet treading upon the realm of Jambudvīpa, her right foot stamps the sky as her multicolored skirt swirls upward; the fire of wisdom blazes forth, filling the void of space, and through recitation and upholding, she attains the stage of non-arising.

The forty-three syllables of the root mantra were empowered by the Tathāgata of the Uṣṇīṣa Light, who personally spoke this gāthā to introduce it. For the sake of all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, world-protectors, and countless others, he requested that the *Pūrṇa-brahmasvara-dhāraṇī* be recited; herein, nine missing syllables from the preceding mantra have been added and inserted.

Oṃ hrūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Mahāpara-vaṇa khuḥ | Kiṃ kiṃ | Hemaṇi | Viji ve | Manaśe | Oṃ caṭara | Uṃ ṣṭramuṃ gaṃ | Haṃ haṃ | Hūṃ hūṃ | Phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. Now add these mantra phrases: Oṃ caṭara hemaṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Having completed the contemplation of non-conceptual samādhi and taken refuge in the Triple Gem, next generate bodhicitta without seeking the fruits of human or celestial realms. May all sentient beings together realize the Unsurpassed Vehicle; may the world of sentient beings and their environment be transformed into emptiness, and may self-māras be dispelled so that the teachings are purified.

Within the moon disc of the mind arising from the four immeasurables is the syllable HŪṂ; light ascends into space, where immeasurable Buddhas arrive. As the reflected image vanishes, the essential body (svabhāva-kāya) emerges as the King of Spirits, adorned with vermilion-tipped hair, his emanation-body (nirmāṇa-kāya) majestic and sublime.

With three faces and nine eyes, holding six precious implements in hand, amidst the blazing fires of the kalpa, he maintains a posture of serene wrath. With the light of *HŪṂ*, the Wisdom Buddha is summoned once more; in a single thought, he arrives, provided with the five kinds of fragrant flowers for ablution, rinsing, and washing the feet.

*Jaḥ hūṃ baṃ hoḥ*: The wisdom syllables are non-dual and one; from the blue heart, throat, and crown, the Buddhas of the ten directions arrive. Nectar is poured as an empowerment, filling the vessel of radiant light; body, speech, and mind are purified—this is the ultimate recitation of me, the Buddha.
Homage to the Original Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha!
Homage to the Emanation Body Śākyamuni Buddha!
Homage to the Great Powerful Divine King Buddha! Recite each ten times.
When reciting the secret mantras with the mind and mouth in harmonious accord—whether a hundred thousand or a million times—one will surely realize the path to Nirvana.

From the left heart, the Great Powerful Spirit-King emanates; majestic and resplendent, he receives homage from neither devas nor humans. A ray of light from between his brows illuminates the worlds of the ten directions, while celestial flower garlands and jeweled canopies appear, and the gods play music as Brahmā, rising from his abode, requests that the Dharma be propagated throughout the world.

At that time, there was a Brahmā King named Jie Shizhu (Saviour of the World) who, leading a host of Brahmās, came to pay homage at the golden coffin containing the body. He looked up and addressed the Great Deity of the indestructible Vajra-body: "The sentient beings are in peril; may the Tathāgata’s compassion emerge!"

The Great Deity spoke, saying: "Listen, Brahmā King, Savior of the World! From the moment I manifested from the golden coffin for seven days, gods and humans have lamented and entreated me to subdue the Śikhin demon, who has arisen with unwholesome intent to assault the Lord of Compassion."

The World-Honored One commanded me to proclaim this to the fourfold assembly so that they may know: do not consider this a minor matter, for how could one escape the mundane world otherwise? When the Tathāgata manifests his parinirvāṇa, the various devas of the four fruits harbor doubts; therefore, he entrusts this scripture to be circulated everywhere, establishing transformation in this turbid age into a pure land and transforming the ordinary physical substance into the Buddha-body.

The assembly of Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, along with the eight classes of devas and nāgas, constantly protect them day and night; having perfected the adornments through the cultivation of precepts, concentration, and wisdom, they first resolve upon Bodhi and realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Dharma-body is without marks; how can birth and death be spoken of? Folly, ignorance, false views, anger, and strife, along with lust, delusion, the fire-house, and the city of doubt—only when one thoroughly penetrates True Suchness will one finally arrive.

The emanated Buddha from the light atop the head proclaims a divine mantra, beginning with the seeking of the first fruit up to the stage of Tathāgata; regarding the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight noble truths—how could there be the principle of day and night across the sun, moon, and four continents?

From compassion, joy, equanimity, and the myriad practices of the six perfections, one suddenly realizes the Buddha’s very marrow within the pure void of *raṃ-ta*. The ten stages and three levels of worthiness are accomplished without departing from this essence; when the faculties of sentient beings are gradually perfected, they become vessels for Buddhahood.

The sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom pervades the entire limit of the Dharma-realm; its brilliant radiance illuminates the greed, hatred, and delusion of sentient beings. Those who are born perceive permanence, while those who die perceive annihilation; yet neither permanence nor annihilation is the ultimate, true message.

The Brahma King Savior of the World, leading the assembly of Brahmās, circumambulated the golden coffin and paid homage toward the Great Deity; as for myself, following the Buddha as we traveled through the ten directions, there has been no Great Sage or Honored One greater than the Vajra-Wielder with the precious mace.

The Divine King proclaimed: "Listen, Brahmā, Savior of the World! From the wisdom of the Perfectly All-Knowing One, I have manifested as the Great Divine King, the Secret Power-Wielder (Guhyapuruṣa). I shall subdue the Śikhin and manifest [the truth] for future sentient beings."

The Forty-two Character Heart Mantra of the Precious Seal Subdues the Mind: All demons and spirits are swept away and return to the world of the East; Śikhin, who was haughty, offered tribute, and as the Buddha entered parinirvāṇa, birth and extinction became signless, and with conditions exhausted, he accorded with tranquil stillness.

The power of the Sugata’s wisdom is beyond comparison for me; the supernatural powers of bodhisattvas and arhats are like the soil on a fingernail, while those of the World-Honored One are inconceivable, like the soil of the great earth. Yet Māra privately considers his own spiritual penetrations to be supreme.

The Tathāgata, having completed his causal conditions, manifested the appearance of entering parinirvāṇa; the māras, arrogant and failing to pay homage to the Tathāgata, were destroyed in their lairs, and those two groups were brought back, causing the gods and humans to cease their grief and distress through the divine vision.

The hearts of the devas and the fourfold assembly were filled with joy; the palaces of the Māra kings all collapsed and crumbled, while his fierce hordes trembled and fell. Yet, perhaps the supernatural powers of the two sages still arose.
The Mara King deliberated: "The Tathāgata has appeared in the world once more, or perhaps those two sages have come to destroy my realm.
Having reflected thus, he realized through his supernatural power that he could not reach them; tears fell from both his eyes as he thought, "Before long, disaster shall arise."

From the mouth of the Emanated Buddha atop his crown, he recited a verse; its radiance illuminated the void of worlds as numerous as motes of dust. The palaces of the Māras of the three realms became like black lacquer; they dared not disobey him, as he gathered sentient beings and departed.

Terrified by this, the eight consciousnesses of Śaṅkhinī are no longer within her body; the factions of the great minister gradually rise upon the earth, and having utterly extinguished the defiled traces of demonic hordes, they all take refuge [in the Dharma]. I only pray that through your compassion you will spare my remaining life and body, and that the two classes of mantra-seers may each return to their supernormal powers.

Fainting and unconscious, there was no path to escape; my soul fled and my courage failed, leaving me unable to speak. Now that the two classes of mantra-sages have each returned their supernatural powers, I gaze upon the Great Deity and am able to return home today.

Great Spirit-Enchanter! Shame on you, you conch-crested demon! You are utterly foolish, arrogant, and addicted to sensual pleasures; yet you do not reform your poisonous heart and continue to offend the Lord of Compassion. You must quickly repent, abandon the heterodox, and return to the correct principle.
If your heart does not repent, seek confession and purification early; otherwise, you will lose your life and fall into Niraya hell.
In your previous lives, you forcibly bestowed wisdom upon sentient beings; now that your merit is exhausted and your pleasures have ended, you shall fall into Niraya hell.

The unwholesome karma of the mind creates offenses as vast as mountain ranges; hundreds of thousands of followers gather together in one place, and hundreds of thousands of millions of people suffer calamities every day, for each individual is followed by the eight consciousnesses and the four serpents.

When the six sense-faculties encounter objects, a single thought may give rise to malice and a lack of compassion; this beckons and entices the multitude of sentient beings, who are then beset by the eighty-eight latent tendencies (*anuśaya*). These hundred afflictions pull one along, further adding twenty evils; thus, throughout the twelve periods of the day, calamities are received from this origin.

With a band of malevolent followers and the celestial Māras as their kin, they entice sentient beings and ensnare them into the assembly of Māra’s faction; tens of thousands at a time meet with calamity and suffer great slaughter, yet only the four elements, the five aggregates, and the six sense-faculties remain as the masters.

The mental consciousness does not manifest, yet the five sense organs are constantly active; the six objects and material phenomena stir with the seven outflows and eight impurities; the nine fetters and ten entanglements drag one along in bondage, giving rise to the twenty-five states of existence and the hundred and eight afflictions.

The eighty thousand afflictions turn their minds at that very moment; the eight consciousnesses are transformed until reaching the path of liberation. Without moving the five aggregates, one realizes the body of the Dharma King; the hundred delusions and inversions are suddenly eliminated, and the hundred dharmas are realized.

The one hundred and twenty evils are transformed into fruits of merit; the eighty-four thousand [afflictions] are transformed into marks of radiance. All are created by your own mind and do not come from external sources; it is like a clear blue sky where no object exists, yet black clouds are stirred up and arise.
Suddenly the clouds disperse, and the sun and moon shine with perfect clarity; though thick darkness and gloom may gather, they are not to be sought from without.
This single mind of yours is fundamentally round and upright; when delusion ends and awakening occurs, the principle within its own substance is not diminished by even a fraction.

Turn back your evil thoughts and immediately return to the Path of Rectitude; offer up precious rain, palaces, and flower garlands to the Tathāgatas of the Dharma-realm, the Bodhisattvas, and the Saṅgha of the four fruits of realization; may devas, nāgas, and worldly lords all enter the Isle of Unconditioned Suchness.

The Brahma King Śaṅkhakuṭa then paid homage to the Great Sage; with tears falling from his two eyes, he prostrated himself on the ground and offered this plea: "I repent for all the transgressions and unrighteous acts committed in the past. Together they raised their voices, saying, "Namo Śākyamuni! and sought repentance from the presence of the two sages, the King of the Śaṅkha-crested ones.

The two classes of mantra-siddhas each returned their supernatural powers and stood solemnly as before, surrounding the divine king. The leader Śaṅkhaja, together with his host, confessed their faults and sought absolution, saying: "O Holy One, have compassion on us and cease to harbor suspicion."

Śaṅkhakeśa addressed him, saying: "Welcome, Great Sage, please take note. In the past, driven by the causes and conditions of my habitual practice of evil deeds, I was harsh and overbearing toward things, harming the bodies of other sentient beings. Now that I have encountered your proclamation of the transformative teaching, I prostrate myself with my head at your feet."

Great Buddhist activities arose within the palace of the Māra King; heaven and earth became clear and serene, while the sun and moon increased in brilliance. Birds and beasts rejoiced as they came to circumambulate the golden coffin, and the twin trees turned white, bowing with reverence to receive his feet in worship.

The Great Power King of Spirits led the hosts of Māra and the Kīṭa-demons; the two sages and their retinues of ministers gazed upon him with reverence together. The fourfold assembly at the Buddha’s gathering, along with the eight classes of beings and all the celestial and terrestrial spirits, each offered respectful salutations and spoke verses in unison.
Various delusive thoughts arise from that ignorance, creating all manner of illusory māras as their retinue.
The Tathāgata instructs and guides others so they do not enter the faction of Māra; he upholds the school and establishes the teaching with a will forever unchanged.

Gold emerging from the ore is obscured by ignorance; oil within flour is forever difficult to extract. When distinguishing between the ore and the oil, the flour is white and the gold is red; yet when abandoning the false to return to the true, the yellow and the white are no longer two different things.
The Dharma-realm universally transforms the three realms and the four modes of birth; it arises solely from the mind and is not to be sought elsewhere.
Having first encountered an enlightened teacher, one does not enter the crooked paths of error; now meeting the Great Awakened One, one is spared from entering the prison of saṃsāra.

The eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and body are fashioned from gold; though the nature of gold remains unchanged through bowls, basins, hairpins, and bracelets, its myriad forms and thousandfold differences reveal the fundamental nature with great clarity. When the nature of gold is melted, it is fixed in true emptiness, functioning with sovereign ease.
When the four māras create obstacles, the Tathāgata’s compassion arises; Mahākāla, the great powerful wrathful one, emerges.
Avalokiteśvara, the Great Wisdom, Lord of the Horse-Necked Hell, does not abandon the gates of entry and comes to rescue sentient beings from their suffering.

The gate of compassion opens, revealing the unconditioned wisdom that saves the world; the clouds of loving-kindness spread everywhere, sheltering those born from eggs, wombs, moisture, or transformation. Those afflicted by malice and wrong views cannot enter the path to Bodhi; even those of high rank and power who ascend together shall all return to the ultimate state.
Upon hearing the verse, the divine king shook his eight arms, cast about with his nine eyes, and stood poised on his right foot.
From within the purple-golden coffin, the square and round fire of wisdom emerged, shattering the illusory arts and annihilating the Śaṅkhacūḍa demon.

The function of this secret chapter is universally bestowed upon the world of the final dharma age; even those who have newly entered the ten wholesome paths and whose mouths are foul with impurity may recite it. When the Buddhas of the ten directions hear the sound of this divine mantra being recited, they will each take note of them, so that they shall proceed directly to the stage of non-explanation in the future.

Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, and Vajragarbha; the Bodhisattvas Śāriputra and Subhūti attained awakening; Maudgalyāyana and Kāśyapa, companions among those of the four fruits of Arhatship—praising him with "Excellent! they offered incense, flowers, and celebratory offerings.

The wrathful Vajra hosts of the devas of the three realms, upon hearing the sound of this mantra, bend their bodies to stand in attendance as guards. Whatever aspirations one may have shall not fail to be fulfilled. For those who have not yet realized the ultimate principle, it swiftly provides the path to Bodhi. By reciting the root mantra, its spiritual efficacy is proven; through the drawing of talismans and seals, or the carving of pestles from fragrant wood, one may test and treat all manner of ailments and other such matters.

Reciting my King of Mantras is like encountering sweet rain during a drought; it is like being defeated in battle and then meeting the arrival of a great general; it is like a solitary and destitute person meeting their parents on the road; it is like an elderly person with a terminal illness finally meeting the physician Jīvaka.

The mantra-reciter must not give rise to doubt; the divine kings will respectfully obey and employ them as directed. Beings in the realms of devas, asuras, hell-beings, and hungry ghosts who hear the sound of the mantra shall all attain liberation.
Even those with malicious intent who maintain this recitation shall obtain extraordinary fruits;

when one is disciplined and focused, with mind and speech in harmonious accord, its other powers will not equal the force of these verses. Virtuous men and faithful women who maintain this recitation shall gain benefit.

When this mantra is written upon silk, paper, or *pātra* leaves, or upon jeweled nets, fine silks, flower garlands, or precious caskets, it shall be protected by the various devas, nāgas, and spirits according to their respective rites; a jeweled canopy shall cover its summit, where the ancient Buddhas sit in serene composure.

If even a single mote of dust from this incantation falls upon an object, and the wind carries that mote to settle upon the body of a sentient being, the merit and reward they shall obtain will be as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; by painting an image of the Crown, they shall be delivered from the Avīci Hell.

With sandalwood craftsmanship and a vajra of profound significance, holding the precious mace at the heart of the maṇḍala, one offers incense, flowers, lamps, ointments, fruits, and food to worship the Great Honored One, the Wrathful Śākyamuni.

Mold fragrant water and clay to sculpt an image of compassion; fashion a beautifully adorned vessel with a hundred ornaments and install a ritual vajra within it. With devotion, perform one hundred thousand recitations while maintaining the mudrā without wavering; when the vajra shakes and the water surges, at that moment you shall attain clear realization.

The mallet-image emitted light, speech, and miraculous transformations; from the left heart of the Great Awakened Compassionate Honored One, these auspicious omens manifested in myriad ways. My heart was filled with great joy, and by the power of my vows, I recited [the mantra] three hundred thousand times once again.

The divine spirit-king manifests spiritual resonance; by reciting and upholding this Dharma discourse, one should prepare a basin filled with pure water and chant my secret mantra without ceasing day or night. When the water surges and the ritual dagger vibrates, one will realize the supernormal power of radiant light.

Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, he constantly recites it with his mind and mouth; when the fruit ripens, he attains mastery in samādhi and communicates through spiritual resonance. All deities of the temples he frequents pay him reverent homage, following him without ceasing and not daring to disobey his noble commands.

The four hundred and four diseases, as well as various spirits, demons, and monsters, and the harm caused by *gudu* poisons and hidden deities that injure the lives of others—may these ailments arising from the past karma of the afflicted person, which produce many cycles of resentment and debt, be forever eliminated and healed through this secret mantra written in vermilion.

The mantra-reciter, through sincere devotion, consecrates the water; it is inscribed with vermilion in forty-two secret square seals, cut, folded, and sealed for protection. Worn upon the body or rolled into pills and taken by mouth, it eliminates all hundred maladies.

No one has transcribed this talisman of the miraculous response of the Precious Seal; it is carved from fragrant wood and inked with sand to stamp upon paper. When used as before by cutting it into pills, its efficacy is peerless, and from the halo upon the crown of the head, emanating Buddhas radiate great beams of light.

The title refers to the past, present, and future; all Buddhas proclaim this root mantra with one voice. From the attainment of enlightenment to nirvana, there is none who does not utter this sound; it is recited by the realms of sentient beings, the four modes of birth, and the six classes of devas and nāgas.
When men and women of pure faith single-mindedly recite these secret sounds, they shall attain the fruit of Buddhahood and all worldly affairs shall be accomplished.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, the Tathāgata gives rise to great pity; he emits light, shakes the earth, and manifests great supernormal powers.
The mantra master shall see the matters they seek appear within their dreams; it universally subdues all previously bound kings of mantras and patriarchs.
For emperors, crown princes, and great ministers of antiquity, as well as for those with physical or mental ailments, there is no response that does not come through the recitation of this mantra.

All [afflictions] are gathered and suddenly eliminated; water surges forth and medicinal light emerges. Upon taking it, one is healed, and the hundred ailments find it difficult to arise again. When the sun and moon are eclipsed, wind and rain do not follow their proper seasons, and the five planets lose their courses, oppressing sentient beings with suffering.

When human calamities, national misfortunes, and years of famine arise, and rebellious thieves break out, causing both ruler and ministers to lose their composure, one should summon the five paths to oversee and record the situation.
Looking up at the void, establish a fixed period for reciting mantras; thus the state shall be preserved in peace and security, and disasters shall never again arise.

The Emperors Wu of the Wei, Zhou, and Tang dynasties destroyed the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha; they prohibited leaving the household life to cultivate practice and realize true nature, and they coerced monks and nuns into returning to secular life with heavy corvée labor. By destroying the fundamental vehicle of the teachings, they were certain to enter the Avīci Hell.

Simply recite the "Precious Jewel" mantra while performing the previously described "Universal Gathering Seal. The bhikṣus, though suffering hardship, shall be transferred to the domain of the evil king; he will then feel remorse and repentance, taking refuge with his heart, so that stūpas and shrines, as well as vihāras and monasteries, shall arise once again.

Using gold, silver, copper, or iron to fashion a dragon-shaped incense seal image, fill a jar or vat with water and cast the image into the water; the Sāgara Dragon will seize and record it with his hand-seal, causing the water to surge, the image to move, and thunder to roar in the sky.

The Muni, the Fire-Transforming Great Power King-Worthy Buddha—reciting these three names of the World-Honored Buddha—sent down a great torrent of sweet rain that drenched all of Jambudvīpa; after long rains had damaged things, he silenced the thunder and brought forth clear skies.

Elephants, horses, camels, oxen, and other beasts difficult to tame; those afflicted by seasonal diseases who merely drink the water of divine mantras; and snakes, rats, and evil insects that damage all manner of others' property—by sprinkling this water upon their dwellings and grounds, these creatures will naturally leave no trace behind.

All prohibitions cannot be fully recounted one by one; I urge you to examine the authentic scriptures with diligence and care. Transcending the mundane and entering the sacred are all within your own mind; failing to realize True Suchness is to go astray and employ the mind in error.

Yakṣas, malevolent spirits, mountain sprites, and terrestrial deities; all shrines of water palaces, rock caves, trees, and stones; and *wangliang* and malevolent demons who have long dwelt among humans—may they all be completely gathered, subdued, and expelled from their invasions of households, states, and capitals.

Golden silkworms, snake-poisons, skull-spirits, golden and silver scorpions, centipedes, and toads—all such classes of *gū* spirits—who cast down death and ruin within food and drink upon the lives of the virtuous: by wearing this Jewel Seal Cloud-Sign (*ratnamudrāmeghacinha*), one shall suffer no harm.

You with the hearts of wolves and the natures of dogs, human-faced beasts—your birth year, month, day, and milk-name are fully known. I write your name in vermilion and tread upon it with the soles of my feet; with my great hands I seize you, and with head bowed in repentance, I prostrate before you.

If one’s mind and intellect are dull and lacking in discernment, yet one seeks the wisdom of the *dhāraṇī-saṃgraha*, one should swallow the mantra-seal and silently bestow great eloquence; thus, through total retention (*dhāraṇī*), one will become widely learned, erudite, and ultimately perfected.

Reciting the name of Anāthapiṇḍada relieves the suffering of poverty; long life and immortality come from precepts, concentration, and bodhi. Bestowing gifts upon sentient beings leads to great nobility and wealth in future lives; it is superior to practicing alchemy for elixirs or refining purple-golden gold.

The physical form of the segmented body undergoes transformation yet remains eternally indestructible; one certainly enters the stage of segmentation while possessing long-lasting mastery over spiritual powers, flying through the air like a bird, coming and going without obstruction, emitting fire from the crown of the head and water from the soles of the feet.

His transformations and unimpeded powers are unfathomable to both sages and ordinary beings; before the image, he recited mantras as prescribed on the mountain retreat, and when his dwelling lacked water, he struck the earth to produce sweet, fragrant water, causing the illnesses of the multitude to vanish instantly.

For those who have long lacked offspring, this secret mantra universally gathers and records [the blessings]; for women afflicted by a hundred ailments or by demonic pregnancies, it extends their years and removes obstructions; when calamities befall one's ancestors, men and women shall practice filial piety and righteousness; and as for ghosts, monsters, and mountain goblins, they shall be immediately pacified and subdued through this mantra-seal.

It dispels afflictions from defilement, transmissible pestilence, and the influence of malevolent spirits or dream-encounters; it enables those who are immensely wealthy to gather further treasures, and if one encounters legal disputes or imprisonment, one shall be released. When facing the clash of battle, rebellious enemies will naturally cease their hostilities.

Regarding the attainment of the Buddha-ground, there is nothing that is not accomplished; it subdues the celestial Māras and the icchantikas upon the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and among all worldly affairs, there is nothing that is not fulfilled. This is the secret speech of the Jewel King, spoken by the Tathāgata who emits light.

The mind-monkey and mental faculties are bound by permanence, bliss, self, and purity; if one's aspirations were not fulfilled, the Sugata would be speaking falsely. Yet the Tathāgata speaks words of truth, words of reality, and his speech is never deceptive regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The gāthās and miraculous efficacies were spoken by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; the śrāvakas, celestial immortals, and seers established seals, talismans, and painted images. Through the power of long-standing great vows and the diligence of dhyāna, even the Brahmins and non-Buddhists became as clear-sighted as polished black lacquer.

How could the Jewel-Vajra Spirit King dare to speak of himself? From the Buddha emanated upon his crown, he proclaimed the divine mantra; with a wrathful body leaping forth, his eight arms grasped various implements, universally emitting immeasurable radiance from hundreds of jewels.

The transformation Buddha atop the crown of his head likewise displays the marks of a Great Man; with palms joined at his mouth as he sits, he emits immeasurable light that reflects and illuminates one another, dispersing and destroying illusory arts and calamities, eliminating defiled traces, and subduing the Śaṅkhakeśa demons.

The devas of the three realms, the Four Great Kings, Tāvatimsa, and others; the asuras of the six paths, the world-dwelling Brahmās, and the hosts of world-protectors—all prostrate with knees bent in reverent salutation, as he proclaims the sound of the perfect secret mantra of supernatural power.

At that time, the Buddha manifested from the light atop the King of Spirits’ head and proclaimed: "The great, vast, and perfectly complete power of spiritual penetrations; the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, has heard the Dharma for the assembly of devas and humans, who have attained the pure Dharma-eye and each realized samādhi."

Sahāmpati and Śaṅkhakuṇḍalī first sent the two assemblies back; surrounded by them from front and rear, they arrived together at the site of Nirvāṇa. The emanation Buddhas and divine kings traveled throughout the ten directions, while the Emanation Buddha preached the Dharma as the sovereign who benefits and delivers sentient beings.

The Great Power Divine King proclaimed to the fourfold assembly: "Listen! Just now, when our Buddha recited the sounds of this divine mantra, the walls and moats of the demon palaces were utterly toppled and left nothing behind; their foul stench was vaporized from afar, transforming into Utpala fruits."

The Buddha of Fundamental Wisdom manifests as hundreds, thousands, and billions of forms; though the eternally abiding Buddha remains whether dwelling or passing away, sentient beings maintain great vows through prayer, and at their place of practice, they dwell in peace within the illusory transformation of the Dharmakāya.

Firmly maintaining his seat as a bhikṣu within the Many-Jeweled Stūpa, he attained sudden realization as the Honored One Śākyamuni; by the power of his vows, he commands those who uphold mantras, attaining the six supernormal powers and the gate of great liberation.

The Spirit King speaks this oath, fearing that people may harbor doubts or suspicions; we only pray that the Tathāgata will examine the reality of the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), act as our witness, and shatter the doubts of all sentient beings, so that they no longer harbor suspicion or fear, and the thunderous voice may be proclaimed once again.

At that time, although the Tathāgata had entered parinirvāṇa in stillness, from his left heart there manifested the radiance of a hundred jewels; the Buddhas of the ten directions emitted light to drench his golden body, a marvel that filled the hearts of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and the four classes of beings with wonder.

The retinue of left-hand ministers with conch-shell topknots and arrogant pride praised him with one voice, their hearts filled with joy. With the eye of the Way, they clearly perceived the principle of emptiness and true suchness, reaching the stages of Equal Enlightenment and Sublime Enlightenment throughout buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust.

From the light atop his head, a transformation Buddha arises with a joyful smile; he issues a proclamation for the assembly of spirit-kings to listen: "The Buddha of Fundamental Wisdom, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, has subdued the *śikhin* demon who causes loss of illumination and performs harmful deeds."

The Emanation Buddha proclaims the Fundamental Wisdom; upon the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the left-handed forceful one with the conch-crested crown emerges. Humans and devas are struck with alarm and doubt as he subdues the celestial Māras; acting on behalf of the Buddha, the Compassion of True Suchness manifests.

The celestial Māra folded his hands and gazed upon the Buddha of Wisdom; as the conditions for his subjects and followers ripened, they were destined to receive their prediction. Within the assembly, those of pure faith each gave rise to the bodhicitta, firmly upholding their vows with a resolve that shall never regress.

The Tathāgata Emitting Light extended his hand and stroked the crown of Śaṅkha’s head, saying: "Excellent! You have well studied how to abandon the heterodox and return to the right path; you have received this prediction and attained realization of the nature of True Suchness. Having changed from the old to the new through the power of courageous and diligent effort, Śaṅkhakeśarāja received this prediction, and his name shall be the Buddha Pure Radiance.

The Brahma King, having received his prediction, came together with these virtuous friends; for sixty billion kalpas they have cultivated the stages of all bodhisattvas, extensively making offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions, and through practice over successive kalpas, they have realized entry into the stage of the Tathāgata.

Śaṅkhajaṭa attained the Buddha Pure Radiance, fully endowed with the ten titles of the Tamer of Men; the Buddha’s lifespan was twenty thousand years, and the sounds of his Dharma were heard by devas and humans, who widely proclaimed and disseminated it through various forms of embodiment as appropriate.

Manifesting as companions of the two vehicles—the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—he immediately reveals the Buddha-body and the ultimate principle of the One Vehicle; from those born from wombs, eggs, moisture, or transformation up to the Bodhisattva vehicle, all wriggling and sentient beings hear the sound of his light.

From the attainment of the first fruit up to the stage of a Pratyekabuddha, through the fulfillment of the ten stages—Dūramgamā, Dharma-meghā, and the mind-abiding of the tenth bhūmi—one achieves the unsurpassed great bodhi of Buddhahood; during the True, Semblance, and Final Dharma periods, the Buddha’s lifespan is twenty thousand years.

After the Tathāgata Prabhāsa entered the samādhi of parinirvāṇa, he successively transmitted his position to a bodhisattva; those such as the ministers and their retinues who have today taken refuge shall, in due order, realize the very body of the Tathāgata Prabhāsa.

That buddha-field is all named the World Without Defilement; the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, and the fourfold assembly have all taken refuge there. It is no different from the Pure Radiance Buddha currently proclaimed here, as they dwell together in the World Without Defilement.

In the stainless world, Bodhisattvas, followers of the Two Vehicles, the eight classes of spirits, and the fourfold assembly listen to the sound of the Dharma; the Tathāgata Radiance proclaims it just as the transformation Buddhas do now: the Great Fulfillment Divine Mantra, the forty-two sacred paths.

After the Tathāgata Viśuddha had completed his causal conditions and entered parinirvāṇa, the fire of samādhi-wisdom cremated his body and collected the śarīra. A jeweled stūpa was erected reaching as high as the Brahma-heaven, serving as a place for gods, humans, and the fourfold assembly to make offerings and cultivate merit.

At that time, Śaṅkhakuṭī and those of her kind who had come with her, having been transformed by the Tathāgata and received his prediction of Bodhi, were filled with joyful vigor and immediately attained the immeasurable vehicle; in a single moment, they extensively performed the work of a Buddha.

The Great Power King listened attentively to the transformation Buddha’s discourse; his heart leaped with joy as he offered praise and prostrations. He announced to the pure assembly and the noble beings with conch-like topknots: "Through the influence of past karma, we have attained this great and virtuous benefit."

The Spirit King further proclaimed: "Our original teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha, manifested his entry into parinirvāṇa out of compassion for this world of the final dharma. Sentient beings, their consciousnesses enveloped and their merit and benefit lost, required the Tathāgata’s emergence to tame those with conch-like topknots through arduous effort."

The head, body, marks, and majestic deportment manifested by me now have emerged from the transformation of the Buddha’s left heart through fundamental wisdom; the Great Fulfillment Divine Mantra is proclaimed by the emanated Buddhas from the light atop the crown, together with the ritual procedures for reciting mantras, the essential nature of meritorious deeds, and the ritual for binding the seals of the Sovereign Deity.

For the "Seal that Universally Gathers Jewels" (Du she bao yin): bend the ring fingers of both hands toward the palms so that the two fingers rest against each other; place the middle finger on the left and the little finger on the right, pinching them at the tips; extend the fingers straight upward with the base of the middle joints resting against the thumbs.

Through the power of mudrās and mantras, all worldly affairs are accomplished; even wicked men and malevolent spirits bow before the mantra-practitioner. Abandoning their malicious and rebellious hearts, they respectfully obey his commands; they dare not disobey, owing to the firm strength of his vow.

For the "Seal of the Prohibited Mountain Treasure": curve the ring finger of the right hand while keeping the four fingers straight and level; advance and retreat seven steps each time, reciting the mantra once for each seal while looking to the left, right, above, and below. By dispersing these mantras and seals, malevolent intentions will naturally cease.

For the Jewel Seal of No-Thunder to quell evil winds, hail, thunderclaps, and prolonged torrential rain: extend the middle, ring, and little fingers; keep the index finger straight up; and press the thumb against the middle joint. With this left-hand seal and mantra, the clouds disperse and the sun’s light emerges.

For sudden illness, perform the "Precious Seal" (*ratnamudrā*) with the right hand as the adornment: bend the index and middle fingers inward toward the palm, keep the other three fingers straight and aligned. This eliminates the five labors and seven injuries; recite the mantra once for each seal, one hundred and eight times in total, and it will be marvelous.

For the Five-Path Jewel Seal (*pañcamārga-ratnamudrā*): bend the two ring fingers toward the palms while all eight fingers stand upright; for those who have died suddenly, place the seal upon the heart and recite the mantra aloud to cause the soul to return to its physical shell.

Evil spirits and ghosts shall desire to violate the master who maintains the mantra; there will be inauspiciousness in their coming and going, and they will pursue and seize those who have fled or absconded. Day and night, thieves shall steal cattle, horses, pigs, sheep, and the like; birds and beasts shall not abandon their intent to prey upon them.

The Spirit King instructed the assembly on how to recognize spiritual friends. Once the five great jewel seals had been faithfully accepted and put into practice, the four authentic seals and the forty-two secret methods were transmitted for circulation through successive generations during the Final Dharma.

The Wrathful King, a manifestation of great sovereign power, emerged; his majestic deportment and movements were no different from those of the original deity. While the essential body of the spirit-king remained in silent meditative absorption, holding his implement without moving, this manifested image of the ritual form suddenly appeared in the void from the essential body of the spirit-king.

Next, two divine kings suddenly arrived through the air, each holding in his hand several *zhang* of *bèiduó* (Bodhi) white cotton cloth. Upon gathering various pigments such as fish glue and alum, they raised their brushes; as soon as they moved them, the images were solemn and complete, without the slightest difference from the original.

Next, two spirit-kings came to circumambulate the golden coffin, weeping and prostrating as they said: "O Wise Buddha, may you know! The calamities caused by the Śikhin have ended; the Buddha has returned to the ultimate reality (bhūtakoṭi). From the left heart, the fundamental spirit-kings manifested have emerged."

The Sovereign Spirit of the Essential Body tamed Śikhin and brought him to submission; he manifested emanations of myself as minor kings to circulate through the final age. His supernatural powers and transformations are known only to the Tathāgata; may he emit light to grant his seal of certification and leave a mark upon the world of ordinary beings.

Next, the emanated spirit-kings surrounded the sovereign spirit-king and paid him homage, saying: "O Holy One, Great Sage, you have caused us to emerge; for the sake of the assembly, you have established these as provisional means to preserve the ultimate reality. We pray that the King will emit light to illuminate and examine these words of truth."

The light from the ūrṇā-kośa of the Tathāgata Śāntasamādhi issues forth from the coffin; the essential-body spirit-king (*svabhāva-devaputra*) shines with the radiance of a hundred jewels. Two paths of jewel-light descend and drench the crown of the transformation-king (*nirmāṇa-rāja*). All Buddhas provide their seal of certification as this [teaching] flows down into the world of ordinary beings. The Tathāgata Śāntasamādhi emits light, and the essential-body spirit-king emits light to drench the crown of the transformation-king.

The Transformation King immediately took up the brush with his right hand and drew forth a sacred image, majestic and dignified, with three heads and eight arms; its nine eyes flashed as it held a lasso, complete in every detail. Upon its crown was the Tathāgata, palms joined in solemn dignity. Following this, the King drew the iconography of the eight-armed form, including the precious seals and numinous talismans.

Standing with the left foot treading upon a jewel and the right leg extended in a *ālīḍha* posture, with eight dragons coiled around his arms and manifesting all manner of miraculous transformations, the essence of each and every one of these divine kings is entirely without difference; as the great assembly gazes upward, light immediately issues forth.

The wisdom of the merit of past lives is depicted upon palm leaves; a seal of wisdom is carved from fragrant wood one inch and eight *fen* in length, with its characters deeply incised, straight, distinct, and finely polished with vermilion. When this seal is impressed upon plain silk, it shall forever be free from calamity and obstruction.

Once the seal of the knowledge of past lives has been applied and the [elixir] has been swallowed, one immediately attains the samādhi of the realization of the transformation of stages; though the illusory body of an ordinary person finds it difficult to realize the gate of dhāraṇī, through this practice of purifying defilements, one suddenly realizes the pure and wondrous mind.

The karmic power of past lives brings forth fruits in the present: upon the hands, feet, heart, and crown of the head are wish-fulfilling jewels; having attained the supreme state, one early on gains wisdom and eloquence; the spiritual clarity of the mind’s eye causes all dharmas to be spontaneously accomplished.

The second is the Seal of Concealment and Unseen Sovereignty; it is carved from fragrant wood one inch and seven fen in length. The method for its circular inscriptions is identical to the preceding, and its unconditioned emptiness and stillness may be compared to the discourse of the Tathāgata.

The third is the seal of manifesting sovereign, unimpeded flight through space: using fragrant wood one inch and five fen long, it is thus empty; with garments upon the topknot and seals and mantras covering the entire body, one wanders through the realms of dust to realize the conduct of a Bodhisattva.

The seal of the secret mantra of sovereign union of spirit and breath is inscribed with vertical characters one inch and two-fifths deep; when dipped in vermilion and impressed upon the heart, it is revered by both humans and non-humans alike—yet those unable to reach emptiness find it difficult to compare or discuss through mere self-reflection.

After the King had finished drawing the four great precious seals, he was able to draw forty-two others for the assembly at a distance; these were formed upon *pātra* leaves as sacred inscriptions, each clearly distinct and not departing from the structure of the Brahmi script.

Next, when the ritual master has finished drawing the talismans and seals of the Transformation Spirit-King, the assembly, filled with both grief and joy, joins their palms and pays homage. They then address the Essential Body and inform the Transformation Spirit-King, saying: "May you and the entire assembly listen as I speak the definitive truth."

In this world of the five turbidities, lust is the root; within the belly, the two viscera—the raw and the cooked—perform the functions of physiology. Hair, fur, nails, teeth, mucus, saliva, pus, and blood, as well as sinews, marrow, bones, and brain—all are nothing but putrid and rank substances.

The sun, moon, and wind sustain the rotation [of the heavens] to form day and night; metal, wood, water, fire, and earth occupy their respective directions and corners with gravity. Rāhu, Ketu, and Candrāpīḍa move through the three lunar mansions; the four *dou* demarcate the boundaries as the seven stars encircle the Northern Dipper.

Jue and Kang constitute the head, with twenty-eight generals; their waxing, waning, and strange transformations preside over human fortune and misfortune. Tiangang, He Kui, and the Purple Qi shine upon people with beauty; in the first of the four heavens, Śakra is the sovereign ruler.

The Great Trichiliocosm manifested by the Buddha of Fundamental Wisdom contains ten billion suns, moons, five planets, and the arrayed lunar mansions; the presiding deities of the directions, calamities, blessings, and climatic conditions—all adversities encountered by sentient beings—are entirely the result of one’s own cultivation.

In the age of the Dharma’s decay, virtuous people must follow among the ranks of the wicked; their lives will be shortened and they will abandon my gate of compassion. Those with the mind of an icchantika will give rise to the intent to harm bhikṣus, yet even when such incantations and seals are urgently employed, it remains as if the Buddha were still in the world.

The Great Powerful Wrathful King of Manifestation announces to you: "Excellent! O Great Compassionate One, you are able to perform this deed; you shall universally fulfill all sentient beings and cause them to equally receive your great gracious bounty. By the power of your great vows and conduct, sentient beings shall obtain benefit. Thus the Fundamental Body Deity-king praises the Subsequent King.

Next, when the two spirit kings had completed their tasks, they personally entrusted the precious seals and numinous talismans to the assembly; the conch-crested one then received the sacred texts and mystic mantras of the Brahmā-script, thereby manifesting the power of the spirit kings who are the fundamental branches of the Buddha’s majestic authority.

By the power of the roots of goodness of charity, the power of the great assembly of worthy sages, and the majestic spiritual power bestowed by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, may this be recited with single-minded devotion and widely disseminated throughout successive kalpas, so that sentient beings in the Dharma-ending age do not suffer great misery.

Next, the King proclaimed the teachings spoken by the Tathāgata Śikhin: "The Great Mantra-King arises from the finger-seals; the five kinds of jewel-seals correspond to the forty-two lunar mansions. Each preserves its divine function for the purpose of subjugation according to your will."

The efficacy of this mantra cannot be fully described; its refined and solemn empowerment issues forth wondrous portents for all deities. Waters surge and waves ripple as the precious vajra flies across and spins; from the ritual image and implements, light radiates forth, and the words are delivered with absolute precision.

In a dream-like meditative concentration, he personally beheld the Honored One Śākyamuni in the form of the Great Powerful Spiritual King of the Dharma, Reward, and Transformation bodies; as he stroked his beard with a wondrous voice, whatever prayers were offered, the spirits merged and the vital energies harmonized, and the five-colored ritual objects vanished, followed by the two spiritual kings.

Next, the two emanated kings emit great radiance; from their crowns, the radiance of the original essence spirit-kings arises. As the two kings mutually pour one another with this light, the emanated transformation kings vanish, and the eight treasures of the original essence spirit-kings are once again raised up.

Once the Transformation King had vanished, the Vīra-deva spoke: "The Wrathful Vidyārāja who was manifested just now has emerged; he is depicted with three heads and eight arms, pressing down upon the stone. His majestic deportment and movements consist of the precious seals and numinous talismans—secret, perfectly luminous, and signless."

The Buddha Śākyajñāna arises from the power of the left mind-force; the Great Expedient (mahopāya) emanations follow in succession as kings descending from space. All the infinite Tathāgatas of the Dharma-realm of empty space emerge from the heart-seal (hṛdaya-mudrā) of Vairocana.

With his śikhā-knots bowed in reverence, he joined his palms and prostrated himself; having received much guidance and protection, he returned to the correct path. All former evil thoughts have been severed today, and he has realized that his own *tathatā* is of one essence with the Buddha.

The Emanation Buddha bestows the prophecy upon Śaṅkhakuñjara, who is free from doubt; having realized the fruit and attained accomplishment, he knows for himself the sensations of cold and heat. The assembly of the Single Practice likewise receives the prophecy of Bodhi; through the compassion of our Buddha, even those belonging to Māra obtain wholesome benefit.
The Malla addressed him, saying: "Śrīvatsa Bodhisattva, listen! This secret chapter shall circulate until the stage of non-retrogression is reached.
The great assembly listening to the Dharma circumambulated the divine king to the right and stood before him, saying: "O Great Sage, today we have finally beheld your traces."

Śaṅkhajaśikha addressed [the Buddha], saying: "The Tathāgata has manifested parinirvāṇa; from his left side, the Śrīdevī transformed, and from the crown of her head, the Tathāgata emerged. My Buddha has spoken the dhāraṇī and the Malla has discoursed on the meaning of the sūtra; we shall protect and disseminate it, not daring to disobey the Buddha’s decree."

Śaṅkhacakravartin made this vow, which the Tathāgata certified and acknowledged: "In the Dharma-ending age, sentient beings will be deceived by celestial Māras and non-Buddhists; I shall manifest divided bodies throughout billions of Jambudvīpas to sweep away demons and spirits, so that sentient beings may be free from calamity and obstruction."

When the Great Devarāja had finished speaking this sutra and mantra, the Tathāgata Eight-Armed Weapon-Crested Radiance vanished; the mass of purple-gold light gradually approached the golden body, and its radiant physical marks entirely entered the Tathāgata’s essence.

The clarity of emptiness is tranquil bliss; the wondrous existence is the void of true emptiness. Kāśyapa dwells among the Chicken’s Foot Mountains apart from the Buddha; observing the inverted conduct of his disciples, he deliberates at dawn: "This must surely be the Tathāgata entering parinirvāṇa soon; having severed all bonds, he returns to empty tranquility to manifest śarīra."

A thousand bolts of fine cotton cloth were used to wrap the body of the Sugata; a golden outer coffin and a silver inner casket spontaneously rose into the air. He traveled through all four gates of the city of Kuśinagara, and as the dhūta ascetic held the firewood, the fire of samādhi ignited spontaneously.

The eighty-four thousand true śarīra relics of the emanation bodies were distributed throughout the realm of sentient beings, and from this, jeweled stupas arose; two portions were first taken away to the heavens and the dragon palaces, while Kāśyapa cremated his physical body upon Maitreya’s appearance in the world.

Having received and practiced with faith, this verse for the circulation according to the sutra prays that all Buddhas, out of their compassionate pity, may forgive my errors and transgressions; it vows that those within the four modes of birth may together realize the seat of Mind-Only—the principle of the lotus palace of the eight consciousnesses, which is truly beyond words.

Having encountered this excellent medicine after many lifetimes of being shrouded in obscurations, I am now fortunate to realize that it was never absent; may all sentient beings, awakening from their delusion, reflect upon themselves to seek liberation—for where else could the fundamental, perfect luminosity ever fail to be sovereign?

The merit of reciting the Buddha’s name benefits all within the Dharma-realm—sentient beings and their physical environment throughout the ten directions without end. Upon hearing the Buddha’s voice, one is instantly severed from the three evil realms; each person should take this upon themselves, for it has always been so from the very beginning.
The Verses of the Sūtra on the Great Powerful Spirit-King Guhyapada conclude.
